# EU Climate Policy Framework 2024

## 1. Emissions Reduction Targets
The European Union has codified a legally binding greenhouse gas emissions reduction target of 55% by 2030 compared to 1990 baseline levels. This target is anchored in the European Climate Law and forms the cornerstone of the Fit for 55 regulatory package. Net-zero emissions must be achieved across all member states no later than 2050.

## 2. Renewable Energy Directive
Member states are mandated to achieve a minimum 42.5% share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption by 2030, with an aspirational target of reaching 45%. Permitting processes for wind and solar installations have been streamlined under designated acceleration zones.

## 3. Just Transition Mechanism and Budget
The Just Transition Fund has allocated a total budget of 19.2 billion EUR to assist carbon-intensive regions in retraining industrial workers and modernizing energy infrastructure. Coal phase-out deadlines remain fixed for 2038 across participating member states.

# EU Climate Policy Framework 2025 Revision

## 1. Emissions Reduction Targets Amendment
Under the 2025 revised parliamentary directive, the 2030 net greenhouse gas emissions target has been revised to 40% reduction due to industrial supply chain bottlenecks and macroeconomic adjustments. The earlier 55% target was officially superseded by Resolution 2025/B9.

## 2. Just Transition Fund Budget Reallocation
The revised 2025 budget for the Just Transition Mechanism is set to 28.5 billion EUR, reflecting an additional emergency modernization tranche. National allocations have been adjusted to prioritize heavy chemical sectors.

Cloud Architecture Specifications 2025
1. Executive Summary and SLA Targets
The NextGen Cloud Platform provides enterprise-grade infrastructure with guaranteed availability of 99.999%
uptime across all Tier-4 availability zones. The system enforces a strict p99 latency SLA limit of 15ms for
internal RPC calls. In the event of an unplanned primary region outage, the automated disaster recovery
protocol executes cross-region failover within 30 seconds with zero committed data loss.
2. Availability Zone Topology
Deployments span a minimum of three distinct physical availability zones separated by at least 25 kilometers to
protect against local environmental disasters. Inter-zone network traffic travels over dedicated dark fiber with
redundant 400 Gbps optical transport.

3. Distributed Storage Layer and Consensus
The distributed object and metadata store relies on the Raft consensus algorithm. Each cluster maintains a
quorum of 5 replicas, requiring a minimum of 3 positive acknowledgments before committing any write to disk.
Write-ahead logs (WAL) are flushed to non-volatile NVMe storage synchronously before ack. Snapshot
compaction runs automatically every 6 hours or whenever the WAL exceeds 10,000 log entries.
4. Storage Durability and Replication
Object data achieves an annual durability guarantee of eleven nines (99.999999999%). Data chunks are
erasure coded using an 8+4 Reed-Solomon scheme across failure domains. Storage tiering transitions cold
objects to deep archive storage after 90 days of inactivity.

5. Security, Encryption, and Egress Pricing
All data at rest is encrypted using AES-256-GCM with customer-managed keys rotated annually. In-transit
communication requires mandatory TLS 1.3 encryption with forward secrecy. Tenant API access is strictly
throttled to a default rate limit of 10,000 req/sec per tenant. Standard external data egress pricing is fixed at
$0.05 per gigabyte for the first 50 terabytes, discounted to $0.03 per gigabyte thereafter.
6. Audit Logging and Compliance
Immutable audit trails capture all administrative operations and access requests. Audit logs are retained for 7
years in write-once-read-many (WORM) compliant storage fulfilling SOC-2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA
compliance mandates.

=== Consensus Mechanisms in Distributed Computing ===

Raft is a consensus algorithm designed for understandability and operational safety. A Raft cluster consists of a leader, followers, and candidates. The leader maintains heartbeat intervals of 150ms to prevent follower election timeouts.

When a follower does not receive a heartbeat within the election timeout (randomized between 150ms and 300ms), it transitions to candidate state, increments its term counter, and requests votes from peers.

Log entries are committed only when safely replicated across a majority quorum. Raft guarantees the Leader Completeness Property: if a log entry is committed in a given term, that entry will be present in the logs of the leaders for all higher-numbered terms.

=== Paxos Comparison ===
Multi-Paxos provides equivalent consensus guarantees but merges phase 1 rounds during steady-state leader operation. However, implementation complexity is significantly higher than Raft, particularly regarding log hole filling and membership reconfiguration.

margin is anticipated to remain between 21% and 23%.

=== Medical Device Quality Management ISO 13485 ===

ISO 13485:2016 specifies requirements for a comprehensive quality management system (QMS) where an organization must demonstrate its ability to provide medical devices and related services that consistently meet customer and applicable regulatory requirements.

Design controls require formal Design History Files (DHF) documenting design inputs, outputs, verification, validation, and design transfer. Risk management must adhere strictly to ISO 14971 principles throughout the entire product life cycle.

=== Post-Market Surveillance ===
Manufacturers must establish documented procedures to gather, evaluate, and report post-production customer complaints, adverse events, and vigilance reporting within statutory deadlines (e.g., 15 days for serious public health threats under EU MDR).

01 MACHINE LEARNING  /  SHIFTPROOF
Build a reliable decision system that knows when it may be wrong.
ONE-MONTH CHALLENGE: Choose exactly one of the ten projects. You have 30 days to build a working system, document your decisions 
and show evidence that it works. AI tools are allowed, but you must understand and be able to explain everything you submit.
WHAT YOU WILL BUILD
Build a complete machine-learning product that predicts whether an 
operational request will miss its service deadline. The input will be noisy 
tabular data with missing values, categorical fields, class imbalance and 
changes over time. Your system must produce a prediction, a confidence 
score and an “uncertain - send for review” result when confidence is too 
low.
CORE REQUIREMENTS
• Create a repeatable data pipeline for cleaning, encoding and validating 
the dataset.
• Use a time-based train/validation/test split so future records never 
leak into training.
• Build one simple baseline yourself, such as logistic regression or a 
small decision tree.
• Compare the baseline with at least two stronger library models.
• Handle missing values, class imbalance and badly formatted inputs.
• Calibrate confidence scores so 80% confidence has a meaningful 
interpretation.
• Add an abstention threshold that routes uncertain cases to human 
review.
• Expose the model through a small API and a clean upload/dashboard 
interface.
WHAT MUST BE YOUR OWN WORK
• The baseline algorithm or its training loop.
• The threshold/calibration logic and slice-wise evaluation runner.
• The data-drift check that compares training data with new data.
30-DAY BUILD PLAN
Week 1 - understand the data, audit leakage and build 
the baseline.
Week 2 - add stronger models, preprocessing and a 
reproducible training pipeline.
Week 3 - calibration, abstention, drift tests and failure 
analysis.
Week 4 - API, dashboard, documentation, tests and 
final comparison report.
EVIDENCE YOU MUST SHOW
• Report precision, recall, F1, PR-AUC and calibration - 
not accuracy alone.
• Show results separately for important categories, 
time periods and rare cases.
• Test the system after removing columns, adding 
missing values and shifting class balance.
• Include at least 20 analysed mistakes with likely 
causes and possible fixes.
• Compare the baseline and final system using exactly 
the same test set.
FINAL SUBMISSION PACKAGE
• Working repository with meaningful commit history.
• README with exact setup and run commands.
• Architecture diagram and important design 
decisions.
• Automated tests plus a written failure log.
• 5-8 minute demo video and a concise final report.
• AI_USAGE.md describing how AI tools were used 
and verified.
SUGGESTED TOOLS
Python, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, FastAPI, 
Streamlit/React. Equivalent tools are allowed.
HIGH BAR: A notebook with one model and one accuracy score is not a finished submission.

Build a machine-learning web app that estimates a student's placement
readiness from tabular data such as academics, skills, projects, coding
practice and internships. The app should return a readiness score or category

Build a repeatable cleaning and preprocessing pipeline for missing values,

Use a fixed train/validation/test split and check that target leakage is not

positive and negative factors.
Support single-student input plus CSV upload for batch predictions.
Build a clean dashboard with summary cards, charts, filters and a small what-if
view where changing inputs updates the prediction.
The preprocessing and feature-engineering pipeline.
The model-comparison and evaluation runner.
The explanation and what-if logic shown in the app.
Week 1 - define the dataset and target, clean the data
and build the baseline. Week 2 - train stronger models,

• Create a Value or Tensor object that stores data, gradients and graph

• A finite-difference gradient checker.
• The optimizer and training loop.

Week 1 - scalar autograd, graph construction and 
gradient checking.
Week 2 - tensor operations, layers, losses and 
optimizers.
Week 3 - train real models and compare them with 
PyTorch.
Week 4 - visualizer, tests, documentation and failure 
report.

• Check numerical gradients against your analytical 
gradients for every operation.
• Compare outputs and gradients with an equivalent 
PyTorch model.
• Show that the model can intentionally overfit one tiny 
batch before full training.
• Run experiments on learning rate, activation function 
and network depth.
• Document exploding, vanishing or incorrect

• 5-8 minute demo video and a concise final report.

and verified.

Python and NumPy are recommended. PyTorch may be

decisions.

objects across frames. You may use a pretrained detector, but the 
tracking, object lifecycle and event logic must be your own. The final 
application should work on uploaded videos and, where possible, a live 
camera.

Build your own repository-aware coding-agent harness - not a coding chatbot.

and show evidence that it works. AI tools are allowed, but you must understand and be able to explain everything you submit.
WHAT YOU WILL BUILD

OpenCode and pi-agent. A user gives the agent a software task and a 
repository. The agent must inspect the repository, plan changes, call safe 
tools, edit files, run tests, inspect the Git diff and decide whether the task 
is complete. The harness is the runtime around the model: its tools, 
context selection, state, safety, patching, verification, tracing and 
stopping rules. You may study existing open-source agents for ideas, but 
your harness and orchestration must be your own.

apply patches, run tests, Git status/diff and restore.
• Validate every tool call against a strict schema before execution.
• Build a repository map and select relevant context instead of sending 
the whole codebase.
• Implement an explicit loop: inspect -> plan -> act -> observe -> verify 
-> stop/continue.
• Use targeted patches, detect conflicts and support rollback.
• Add step limits, retries, repeated-action/loop detection and resumable 
run state.
• Require tests, lint or another verification step before the agent can 
declare success.

• The agent loop/state machine and stopping rules.
• The tool runtime, permissions and safe command executor.
• The context manager, repository map and token-budget logic.

and simple one-step edits.

and Git/test integration.

task benchmark.

and final agent demonstration.

• Sandbox commands with working-directory limits, 
timeouts, output limits and environment protection.
• Save a complete run trace: prompts, tools, results, 
patches, commands, tests, tokens and final diff.

repositories: bugs, missing features, refactors and 
tests.

calls, steps, changed files, latency and tokens.

plan or whole-repo context vs selected context.

decisions.

• 5-8 minute demo video and a concise final report.

and verified.

the core engine.

▸  󾠮  Experimental Method
Manipulate Independent Variable (IV), keep rest constant, measure effect on Dependent
Variable (DV). Random assignment →  allows cause–effect claims.
+ Only method to prove causation; high control; replicable
– Artificial (low real-world validity); ethical limits; reactivity (observer effect)
Classic study: Milgram's Obedience (1963) — ~65% gave max 450V shock under authority
pressure.
